output.brief: The August dip was almost entirely caused by the cooling failure on floors 6-8. Chiller CH-2 was down 4-19 August. Rooms ran at 26-29 C. Floors 6-8 comfort fell from 8.4 to 6.1. Their overall score fell to 6.8 for checkouts during the outage and recovered to 8.4 once it was fixed. Floors 1-5 were flat. Heat made up 56 of 74 negative comments, all from floors 6-8. The survey method was unchanged. Cleanliness scores and inspection pass rates held steady, and kiosk use, queue times and check-in scores were stable. So the evidence doesn't support blaming either Orrin or the kiosks, and I would not serve notice or pull the kiosks. The deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers is a likely contributing origin. The part had an 11-day lead time and no spare was on site. The 6% rate rise may have added a little to the value dip on floors 1-5, but that is within normal August variation, so I would not reverse it yet. Do not exclude the floor 6-8 responses from the reported score, because that would hide the problem. Next: reinstate chiller maintenance, hold critical spares, and write a guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages. Guests were already apologised to and credited, so a further return-stay offer is optional. I'm fairly confident in this diagnosis, and I did not collect any further evidence.
